svg.title: ESP32-S2 Mini · one-servo AA prototype
svg.desc: One continuous illustrated assembly map: switched four-AA alkaline holder, 5 V buck-boost module, breadboard power rails, S2 Mini beside breadboard, and MG90S servo. Raw battery connects only to converter input. USB remains unplugged. All connections have numbered wire labels.
svg.text: One battery pack. One servo. Every wire.
ESP32-S2 Mini · DAIERTEK switched 4-AA holder · Teyleten 5 V buck-boost · breadboard rails
Top views, enlarged for clarity. Follow terminal labels; drawing is not to scale. Confirm your board matches the reference.
Built-in switch → both electronics and servo
4 alkaline AAs ≈ 6 V nominal. Cover shown removed.
Follow the + / − moulded inside the actual holder.
5 V version · verify output with your meter
EN / PS / ADJ unused. No adjustment screw.
Power pads are soldered; do not bridge selectors.
Rows a–e join; rows f–j join.
Board beside breadboard; female jumpers on headers.
Both header rows must not share breadboard strips.
Male jumper pins enter the servo’s female plug.
Check polarity. Start with the horn unloaded.

svg.text: 1 Remove cells while soldering and inserting jumpers.
2 Disconnect S2 and servo. Measure + rail to − rail: about 5.0 V.
3 Power OFF, connect S2 and servo, then switch ON for an unloaded test.
Rail numbers P/G count holes from the top. Main rows use a–j / 1–63.
USB PROGRAMMING: DISCONNECT THE S2’S THREE JUMPERS FIRST
The S2’s 5V/VBUS pin is directly connected to USB power.
Turning the holder OFF alone does not isolate the servo rail from USB.
Never connect raw battery voltage to 5V/VBUS, 3V3, or GPIO.
Cosmetic internals simplified. Hardware load test and actual-board match pending.
Sources: WEMOS S2 Mini V1.0.0 pinout/schematic · Amazon B09N1GDWQ9 / B0GCW44FDL · TowerPro MG90S. Reference build, not a certified assembly.
